name: Proper activation of disinfection function based on DUT date-time

description:
The test verifies that disinfection is performed at the selected day and hour.
        Test modifies DUT date-time and verifies that the disinfection function is activated
        at the proper day of the week and time.
        Test also verifies that after schedule change the original schedule is no longer executed and after setting 
        [DHW_legionella_enabled] to False despite of that setting schedule disinfection function is not activated in setting date time.

steps.description: Activate P1P2 simulator, reboot MMI and wait for state NORMAL in MMI.
steps.expectation: State NORMAL is reached in defined timeout.

steps.description:
Gradually change the value of [DHW_legionella_enabled] and
             set the value to MMI for each change. For each set value execute steps 3) - 9).

             every day at a random time. Set each generated program to MMI and perform steps 4) - 8).

             set [DHW_legionellaFG] to default value to ensure that the DHW logionella operation will be

               in setting date time.

             according to setting of [DHW_legionella_enabled] in setting date time.

steps.description: Activate P1P2 simulator and wait for state NORMAL in MMI.
steps.expectation: State NORMAL is reached in MMI.

steps.description:
Set all malfunction flags ([error FG], [Warning FG], [Caution FG]) to False
             in P1P2 simulator to ensure no malfunction occur in MMI.
steps.expectation:
All malfunction flags are set to False in MMI, so
             they are correctly transferred from P1P2 simulator.

steps.description: Clear malfunction history to ensure the entire history is empty.
For each malfunction type (Error, Warning, Caution) do steps 5) through 8)
steps.expectation: All subtests pass

steps.description: Generate random values for [error_code] and [error_detailed_code] and set them to P1P2 simulator.
steps.expectation:
[error_code] and [error_detailed_code] are set to generated values in MMI, so
             they are correctly transferred from P1P2 simulator.

steps.description: Read out all malfunctions from malfunction history after introducing no malfunction to system.
steps.expectation: [error_code] and [error_detailed_code] are not set to malfunction history.

steps.description: Set [error FG], [Warning FG] or [Caution FG] (based on type) to True in P1P2 simulator.
steps.expectation:
[error FG], [Warning FG] or [Caution FG] is set to True in MMI, so
             it is correctly transferred from P1P2 simulator.

steps.description:
Read out all malfunctions from malfunction history
             to detect whether generated error code and error detailed code
             were correctly written to malfunction history after introducing malfunction to system.
steps.expectation: [error_code] and [error_detailed_code] are correctly set to malfunction history.

steps.description: Clear malfunction history to ensure the entire history is empty for next subtest.

name: Storing of malfunction in the malfunction history after the change of malfunction code and check of overflow

description:
Test verifies correct setting of malfunction to malfunction history
        when the malfunction flag stays True and error code and subcode change.
        Also checks correct behavior when new malfunction is added to full history.

steps.description: Activate P1P2 simulator and wait for state NORMAL in MMI.
steps.expectation: State NORMAL is reached in MMI.

steps.description:
Set initial conditions which are needed for correct testing of storing malfunctions
             to malfunction history.
For each malfunction type (Error, Warning, Caution) do steps 4) through 9)
steps.expectation: All subtests pass

steps.description: Set [error FG], [Warning FG] or [Caution FG] (based on type) to True in P1P2 simulator.
steps.expectation:
[error FG], [Warning FG] or [Caution FG] is set to True in MMI, so
             it is correctly transferred from P1P2 simulator.

steps.description: Clear malfunction history to ensure the entire history is empty.
Do multiple times (more than 20 to ensure history overflow) steps 7) and 9)
Generate random malfunction (error code, subcode, date-time).
steps.expectation:
Generated [error_code] and [error_detailed_code] are not the same as the previous ones.
             This verification is necessary because if the same malfunction is generated in succession,
             it will not be stored in the history because no change will occur.

steps.description: Set generated [error_code] and [error_detailed_code] to P1P2 simulator.
steps.expectation:
[error_code] and [error_detailed_code] are set to generated values in MMI, so
              they are correctly transferred from P1P2 simulator.

steps.description:
Read out all malfunctions from malfunction history
             to detect whether generated error code and error detailed code
             were correctly written to malfunction history after introducing malfunction to system.
steps.expectation: [error_code],[error_detailed_code] are correctly set to malfunction history (including new malfunction).

name: Persistence of malfunction history

description: Test verifies persistency of malfunction history through reboot.

steps.description: Activate P1P2 simulator and wait for state NORMAL in MMI.
steps.expectation: State NORMAL is reached in MMI.

steps.description:
Set initial conditions which are needed for correct testing of storing malfunctions
             to malfunction history.
Prepare 20 errors and 20 warnings / cautions. Any two subsequent codes should not be identical.
Clear malfunction history to ensure the entire history is empty.
Set each code to P1P2 simulator and let the malfunction to propagate.
steps.expectation: Correct errors and warnings / cautions are present in malfunction history.

steps.description: Power cycle the MMI
Read out all malfunctions from malfunction history
steps.expectation: Correct errors and warnings / cautions are present in malfunction history.

name: Storing of warning
caution and error malfunctions in the malfunction history together

description: Test verifies correct setting of warning, caution and error malfunctions to malfunction history.

steps.description: Activate P1P2 simulator and wait for state NORMAL in MMI.
steps.expectation: State NORMAL is reached in MMI.

steps.description:
Set initial conditions which are needed for correct testing of storing malfunctions
             to malfunction history.
Clear malfunction history to ensure the entire history is empty.
Do many times (to ensure history overflow) steps 5) through 10).
steps.expectation: All subtests pass

steps.description: Set [Warning FG], [Caution FG] and [Error FG] to False in P1P2 simulator.
Generate random malfunction (type, error code, subcode, date-time).
Set DUT time to match next malfunction time (emulate time between malfunctions).
Set generated [error_code] and [error_detailed_code] to P1P2 simulator.
steps.expectation:
[error_code] and [error_detailed_code] are set to generated values in MMI, so
              they are correctly transferred from P1P2 simulator.

steps.description: Set [Warning FG], [Caution FG] or [Error FG] (based on generated type) to True in P1P2 simulator.
steps.expectation:
[Warning FG] or [Caution FG] is set to True in MMI, so
             it is correctly transferred from P1P2 simulator.

steps.description: Read out all malfunctions from malfunction history
steps.expectation: [error_code],[error_detailed_code] are correctly set to malfunction history (including new malfunction).

steps.expectation: State NORMAL is reached in defined timeout.

steps.description: Set [WLAN_cloud_connection] to False and [Eq3_Unified_connection_status] to False in MMI to ensure that communication error occurs.
steps.expectation: Cloud communication error occurs as it is expected after setting required conditions.

steps.description: Set [MR_EmergencyActivationTimer_min], [MR_EmergencyIntermittentOnTimer_min] and [MR_EmergencyIntermittentOffTimer_min] to 1.
Wait for passing [MR_EmergencyActivationTimer_min] and read out value of [MR_dbg_ProcessMode] from MMI.

steps.description: Read out values of SW thermostat input A and SW thermostat input B from MMI.
steps.expectation: SW thermostat input A is active and SW thermostat input B is not active.

steps.description:

             and read out values of SW thermostat input A and SW thermostat input B from MMI.
steps.expectation: SW thermostat input A is active and SW thermostat input B is not active.

steps.description:
Wait 2 seconds for [MR_EmergencyIntermittentOffTimer_min] to be active
             and read out values of SW thermostat input A and SW thermostat input B from MMI.
steps.expectation: Both items SW thermostat input A and SW thermostat input B are not active.

name: Firmware update rollback

description:
The test verifies the rollback functionality of the update process when firmware uploaded during
        the update does not confirm its own validity.

steps.description:
Insert medium with valid instruction file (containing reboot = 1)
             and *.bin + *.crc files from different than current version.
Execute a power cycle to start the update process.
steps.expectation: FW update procedure is started after approx. 5 seconds.

steps.description: Wait for the FW update procedure to finish.
steps.expectation: Target version of the application is running.

steps.description: Read out FW crc.
steps.expectation: Running FW crc is same as expected one (the new one).

steps.description:
| Prevent the new partition from confirming its validity (MMI_PGG_A02_3c).
             | Execute a power cycle within the confirmation time window from boot (x=5 seconds).
steps.expectation: Original version of the application is running. Verify the contents of the memory partitions.

steps.description: Read out FW crc.
steps.expectation: Running FW crc is same as expected one (the old one).

steps.description: Wait for the FW update procedure to start.
steps.expectation: FW update is initiated again.

steps.description: Check generated log files on the medium.
steps.expectation: Logs should contain correct contents.
